findings.title: DeepSeek ignores max_completion_tokens, so the adapter's output bound does not bound DeepSeek
findings.evidence: Non-streaming curl, thinking at default: max_completion_tokens 8 gave 15 completion tokens and finish_reason stop. max_tokens 8 gave 8 completion tokens and finish_reason length. In the adapter's own probe, whose bound is 64, DeepSeek produced 122 output tokens. DeepSeek's API reference documents max_tokens only.
findings.impact: Cost and runaway-output protection cannot rely on the request bound for DeepSeek, or for any compatible server that only knows max_tokens. The default output cap in thinking mode is 64K tokens (documented), which at DeepSeek's prices is a few cents at worst. The host budget gate still applies.
findings.suggestion: Send max_tokens as well as, or instead of, max_completion_tokens for the openai-compatible kind (OpenAI's newer models reject max_tokens, so the OpenAI kind should keep max_completion_tokens). The replay test the_adapter_sends_max_completion_tokens_not_max_tokens pins today's behavior so the change is deliberate.

findings.title: Thinking is on by default and the adapter cannot switch it off or set its effort
findings.evidence: deepseek-flash reasons unless the request says thinking disabled or reasoning_effort none. The probe call carried 81 reasoning tokens of 122 output tokens. The wire shows reasoning in delta.reasoning_content, which the assembler ignores, so reasoning text is never part of the Turn or persisted, matching the design note in request.rs. Reasoning tokens are counted inside completion_tokens, and so are billed at the output price. With thinking disabled through a test-only request field, both turns of the tool round trip worked.
findings.impact: Works, but output cost includes hidden reasoning, and a loop cannot choose to turn it off for DeepSeek. ModelRequest and the profile have no provider-specific request fields.
findings.suggestion: Add an optional per-profile extra request body (merged last, as openai::request_body already supports through its extra argument) so an operator can set thinking or reasoning_effort.

findings.title: DeepSeek documents that reasoning_content must be sent back with tool calls, but today it was not enforced
findings.evidence: The DeepSeek thinking-mode guide says that for requests with tools the reasoning_content must be passed back in all later requests, and that omitting it returns HTTP 400. On 2026-11-02 two follow-up turns, built by the neutral ModelRequest (which has no field for reasoning), were accepted with 200. One followed a tool turn with no reasoning, the other followed a turn with 48 real reasoning tokens (deepseek-reasoned-turn-1 and -2).
findings.impact: Multi-turn tool use works today without reasoning_content on deepseek-flash. DeepSeek may start enforcing its documentation, or enforce it for other models, so a 400 on a follow-up is a plausible future failure. This observation is for one model on one day.
findings.suggestion: Keep the live test live_deepseek_follow_up_after_a_reasoned_tool_call_default_thinking as the canary. If it starts failing with a 400, either pass reasoning back inside a provider-private field of the profile or disable thinking for DeepSeek profiles (F2).

findings.title: deepseek-chat is an undocumented alias
findings.impact: Anyone who configures deepseek-chat today gets deepseek-flash and its pricing. DeepSeek can retire the alias.
findings.suggestion: Document deepseek-flash as the compatible-profile example for DeepSeek.

findings.title: Pricing depends on time of day and the repository has no DeepSeek price record
findings.evidence: DeepSeek's pricing page lists off-peak and peak rates (peak is 01:00 to 04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC on weekdays, excluding Chinese public holidays. Off-peak is half the peak rate). crates/agent/src/cost.rs holds prices for gpt-5.4-nano and claude-haiku-5-5 only, so estimate_micros returns NoPrice for DeepSeek.
findings.impact: A budget gate that meters a DeepSeek profile would see NoPrice. The live test computes cost from its own table. No production code changed.
findings.suggestion: If DeepSeek becomes an agent profile, add a deepseek-flash entry priced at the peak rate, which is the safe upper bound.

findings.title: Documented but unobserved: 402 Insufficient Balance is classified as Other
findings.evidence: DeepSeek's error-code page documents 402 as Insufficient Balance. openai::classify_status maps 429 with a quota code to Quota, but any 402 falls to HttpClass::Other, which normalizes to provider_refused, Terminal, no cost. Not observed live, because it needs an empty balance.
findings.impact: Safe (terminal, never retried) but not labeled as exhausted quota, so any later operator alert or user message keyed on provider_quota_exhausted would miss a DeepSeek account that ran dry.
findings.suggestion: Map 402 to Quota in classify_status and add a unit test beside live_credit_exhausted_is_quota_not_retryable.

unrelated_windows_failure.observed: Fails every time on this Windows 11 machine (6 of 6 runs) at replay.rs:134. The error's acceptance is Uncertain where the test expects Accepted.
unrelated_windows_failure.unchanged_code: Nothing in crates/agent/src or in replay.rs was changed on this branch. The failure is present on the base revision.
unrelated_windows_failure.likely_cause_unverified: The replay server's DisconnectAt closes the socket with SO_LINGER 0 (an RST). On Windows an RST can discard bytes the client has not read yet, so the client may see the reset before the response headers. That would classify the failure as Uncertain instead of Accepted. This was not confirmed.
unrelated_windows_failure.tracking: Falls under issue #3 (run the S03 tests on Windows).
